class.name: SnowPowderCloud3D
class.brief_description: Draws an avalanche's powder cloud as a heavy gas in NVIDIA Flow.
class.description: [SnowAvalanche3D] adds one of these and works out where a fast, dry front blows snow into the air, how much, and where it settles. This node draws that snow through a pool of sphere emitters on the front, in a [code]PhysXFlow3D[/code] of its own. The gas is heavier than air, rests on the terrain, and drifts with the weather's wind. It reaches the PhysX module only by class and property names, so without Flow it draws nothing and everything else behaves the same.

method.name: get_active_sources
method.description: How many emitters are blowing snow now.

method.name: get_flow
method.description: The [code]PhysXFlow3D[/code] that draws the cloud, or [code]null[/code] before the first cloud or without Flow.

method.name: has_flow
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once a Flow simulation is in place.

members.member: If [code]false[/code], nothing is drawn. The avalanche still lofts and settles the snow.
How much heavier than air the cloud is, as Flow's negative smoke buoyancy. Suspended snow is 3 to 10 kg/m³, against air's 1.2.
The number of emitters along the front. Each overlaps its neighbours, and the weaker parts of the front feed at least a third of the strongest, so the cloud rises as one wall.
Emitter smoke per kg/s of snow blown into the air.
The terrain the cloud rests on, Flow's terrain floor. The avalanche sets it to the snow cover's height source.
The share of the front's speed that blows up out of it, the eruption current.
